section.form_description: One enthusiasm followed all the way down. The narrator opens on a subject they love and know cold — how a mass relay actually throws a ship, the grammar of their homeworld's oldest language, the breeding lines behind a varren pit — and talks it out well past where a listener would have stopped them, then follows a seam into the next subject and the next. An infodump, but a personal one: every fact is here because the narrator went and got it, and why they cared runs under the telling — the childhood that started it, the person who taught them, the love and the plain curiosity of it. Sections are subjects, each opening where the last one's tangent left off.
section.form_note: Rewritten after feedback. The brief is one enthusiasm talked out at length, which is tunnel; but the spine is topical and associative, not Shepard's playthrough. The order is a chain of thoughts, each section opening from an object, a feeling or an aside in the one before (a dated fragment -> the ruins the Protheans themselves dug up -> the empire -> the neighbours nobody excavated -> a goddess who was a guise -> what other species made of them -> the Mars cache -> a message meant for someone else's mind -> her own dig -> the fall and the shelters -> the Crucible -> the cycles before -> the arithmetic of a cycle -> what to leave). Nothing runs in game order; Shepard's encounters (Eden Prime beacon, Therum, Feros, Ilos, Thessia, Javik, the Leviathan trail) appear as evidence or anecdote inside a topical section, and where Liara was not there (Eden Prime beacon, the Leviathan trail; Feros and the Presidium hanar dispute she did attend, per Thomas) she draws on Shepard and on her own Shadow Broker network (she is the Broker), saying which source she is using, not merely asking Shepard. Canon kept: Shepard was marked by the beacon, Javik came aboard, the Leviathan DLC and Thessia as recorded; Legion/Tali branches and the ending are not touched, and the talk stops short of the final choice. Pre-Prothean material comes only from corpus pages (Inusannon, thoi'han/Eingana, the Leviathan of Dis, the Leviathans, the Crucible design history) and is hedged in her voice: the corpus dates the Inusannon at 127,000 years and the Protheans at 68,000-48,000 BCE, which does not fit a tidy fifty-thousand-year cycle, and she should worry at that rather than resolve it. target_words is pinned at 9000 (a one-hour spoken lecture at roughly 150 words a minute, pauses included).

required_facts.fact: In 2185, Dr. Amanda Kenson, a human scientist from the University of Arcturus, leads a secret research initiative called "the Project" into batarian space to investigate rumors of Reaper technology. Her team discovers an ancient mass relay in the Bahak system that predates the Protheans—the "Alpha Relay"—and an embedded Reaper artifact called "Object Rho" hidden in an asteroid near the relay. Exposure to Object Rho's visions convinces Kenson and her team that the Reaper invasion is imminent, arriving within days. The team devises an audacious plan: destroy the Alpha Relay by ramming a large asteroid into it, delaying the Reapers' entry into the galaxy by forcing them to find an alternate mass relay route. When Kenson is captured by batarian authorities and charged with terrorism, Admiral Steven Hackett asks Commander Shepard to rescue her. Shepard infiltrates the batarian prison on the planet Aratoht, frees Kenson, and fights through security forces to escape with her aboard a commandeered shuttle. During the escape, Kenson reveals the full scope of the discovery: Object Rho's visions, the imminent Reaper arrival in approximately two days, and the Project's plan to destroy the Alpha Relay. However, upon reaching Project Base on the asteroid, Shepard discovers that prolonged exposure to Object Rho has indoctrinated Kenson and her entire research team. The indoctrinated scientists, now serving the Reapers, attempt to prevent the relay's destruction. Shepard battles through the facility, fighting indoctrinated researchers and security forces while the countdown to Reaper arrival ticks down. Kenson attempts to sabotage the Project's propulsion systems by overheating the fusion reactor, but Shepard manages to override the systems and activate the Project, sending the asteroid on a collision course with the Alpha Relay. Kenson, lamenting that she can no longer "hear the whispers" of the Reaper artifact, triggers a detonator that obliterates her body as Shepard escapes the base. Seconds before the asteroid impacts the relay, the Collector General—possessing the Harbinger Reaper—appears via hologram to confront Shepard about the futility of resistance. The asteroid impact tears the Alpha Relay apart, causing a catastrophic explosion of supernova proportions that annihilates the entire Bahak system, killing over 300,000 inhabitants of Aratoht and devastating batarian space. The destruction delays the Reaper invasion but at an enormous cost. The incident becomes a flashpoint of controversy: while the destruction slows the Reapers' advance, it also claims the lives of hundreds of thousands of batarian civilians and creates a massive power vacuum in batarian space. The destruction of the Alpha Relay becomes the most destructive military action in galactic history and fundamentally alters the balance of power in the galaxy.

beats.text: With Fehl Prime rebuilt and fitted with an anti-ship cannon and kinetic barriers, Captain Toni sends Delta Squad to trace a jamming signal on the colony outskirts. The asari anthropologist Treeya and the colonist Messner come along; Messner lends them his Mako.

At the source they find an unknown alien device. Essex destroys it with his biotics, to Treeya's annoyance. Treeya takes a fragment and leads the group to a functioning Prothean communication system, which she uses to call her mentor Liara T'Soni. Liara guesses the device may be Reaper technology before the link is jammed.

Treeya tells the squad she has doubts — Liara once worked with Commander Shepard and is fixated on Reaper myths. As they head back, the new jamming source flies overhead: a Collector ship, bearing down on the colony. Its Seeker Swarms paralyze the colonists, Captain Toni, Christine and April among them; only Delta Squad, Treeya and Messner, still out at the relay, stay free.

scenes.title: Object Rho and Kenson's True Allegiance
scenes.where: Project Base on a Bahak system asteroid

beats.text: On the asteroid, Kenson showed Shepard the countdown clock: the Reapers would arrive in just over two days. She escorted Shepard through the facility, explaining the Project was ready to proceed with destroying the Alpha Relay.

At Object Rho, Shepard examined the exposed Reaper artifact. Kenson assured the Commander that a minute of exposure would provide all the proof needed. Visions of Reaper invasion flooded Shepard's mind.

While Shepard reeled from the experience, Kenson drew an M-4 Shuriken and pointed it at the Commander. Project guards rushed in. Kenson revealed that she and the entire Project staff had been indoctrinated through prolonged exposure to Object Rho; they now served the Reapers and would do anything to prevent Shepard from stopping the relay destruction.
Shepard moved quickly, disarming Kenson and breaking her wrist. Kenson limped away, holding her arm and ordering her guards to kill the Commander.

Shepard fought through waves of Project guards. Kenson's voice came over the intercom, but Shepard pressed forward until sedative gas incapacitated them. As Shepard lost consciousness, Kenson's eyes glowed with Collector influence.

Hours later, after increased sedative doses failed to keep Shepard under, the Commander woke and fought through the facility. Kenson tried to rally her guards, but Shepard reached the Project Control Room and reactivated the asteroid's engines.
Kenson cut Shepard's communications and raced to the reactor core to destabilize it and destroy the asteroid herself. Shepard intercepted her and activated the cooling rods, preventing a meltdown.

Shepard pursued Kenson to the master control panel. In a frenzy of rage and anguish, Kenson wailed that she could no longer "hear the whispers" and blamed Shepard for their situation. She pulled a detonator, lamenting that they only had to stay asleep. Shepard ordered her to step away, but Kenson pressed the detonator. The explosion obliterated her body and knocked Shepard backward.

evidence.text:
The Alpha Relay was a mass relay in the Bahak system of the Viper Nebula. It was named "Alpha" by Dr. Amanda Kenson and her research team, who determined it was the oldest known mass relay in the galaxy. Outwardly it appeared to be a standard relay, but it was unusual in range and versatility: it normally sent and received mass at the range of a secondary relay, but with certain controls adjusted it could draw on an unprecedented amount of dark energy to send cargo to sixteen other relays and even across a great distance to the Citadel. The Batarian Hegemony had long known of this capability and covered it up to avoid retaliation by other races who would see the relay as a threat.

After discovering the Reaper artifact Object Rho embedded in a nearby asteroid, Kenson's team learned the Reapers would soon arrive in the system and use Alpha to coordinate a galactic invasion. The team concluded Alpha had to be destroyed, even though this would kill more than 300,000 batarian colonists, because its loss would force the Reapers to detour and delay their arrival by months or years. They established Project Base on the Object Rho asteroid, smuggled in engines and navigation systems from Omega, and planned to ram the asteroid into the relay. Before they could act, the team was indoctrinated by Object Rho. During the events of Arrival in 2185, Commander Shepard activated "the Project" despite Kenson's attempt to sabotage the asteroid's propulsion. The asteroid struck the Alpha Relay and tore it apart, producing an explosion comparable to a supernova that wiped out the Bahak system. In Mass Effect 3, if Shepard did not attempt to rescue Kenson, a wounded batarian reveals that the Alliance destroyed the Alpha Relay to delay the Reaper invasion.

evidence.text:
Arrival was the assignment in the Mass Effect 2 DLC of the same name, added after the Horizon mission. Admiral Hackett contacted Commander Shepard privately in the captain's cabin and asked, as a personal favor and alone, to infiltrate a batarian prison on the planet Aratoht in the Bahak system of the Viper Nebula and rescue Dr. Amanda Kenson, an Alliance deep-cover operative and scientist who claimed to have found proof of an imminent Reaper invasion via a Reaper artifact in the system. Kenson had been arrested on terrorism charges.

Shepard fought or sneaked past batarian prison guards and War Beasts, overheard that Kenson's people had planned to crash an asteroid into a mass relay, and freed Kenson from an interrogation chamber. Kenson temporarily joined as a squadmate, hacked an escape route, and the pair stole a shuttle. Aboard it, Kenson explained "the Project": a plan to destroy the local Alpha Relay by crashing an asteroid into it before the Reapers arrived and used it to spread across the galaxy, an act that would trigger a supernova-like explosion destroying the entire system and its colony of 300,000 batarians. She said the artifact, Object Rho, had given her Reaper visions like Shepard's from the Prothean beacons.

At Project Base, a countdown clock marked time until the Arrival. Exposure to Object Rho revealed that Kenson and her whole team were indoctrinated; Kenson drew a weapon, and Shepard was forced to fight through waves of Project personnel and a YMIR Mech before being knocked out and confined to a med lab. Shepard escaped, reached the Project control room, activated the engines to send the asteroid toward the relay, and pursued Kenson to the reactor core to stop her from causing an eezo meltdown. Cornered, Kenson detonated herself, knocking Shepard unconscious and advancing the clock. Shepard fought across the asteroid's surface to a comm relay, was addressed by Harbinger, who declared "Prepare yourselves for the Arrival," and was retrieved by Joker and the Normandy moments before the asteroid destroyed the Alpha Relay. The Bahak system and its 300,000 inhabitants were destroyed, and the Reaper invasion was delayed. Aboard the Normandy, Hackett debriefed Shepard in person, warned that the batarians would seek blood and that Earth would eventually call Shepard to answer for the deaths, but affirmed Shepard had done the right thing.

In Mass Effect 3, if a Mass Effect 2 save lacked this completed assignment, the Alpha Relay was still destroyed but blame shifted to the Alliance's 103rd Marine Division, which suffered casualties reducing its War Asset value, and dialogue changed with Balak, Ghorek, and Anderson.

evidence.text: Admiral Hackett contacts Commander Shepard to ask for help rescuing Dr. Amanda Kenson, an Alliance deep\-cover operative in batarian space who has come across evidence that a Reaper invasion is imminent. Hackett explains that Kenson was recently captured by batarians and charged with terrorism. Wanting to avoid a diplomatic incident with the Batarian Hegemony, Hackett requests Shepard go in solo and rescue the scientist as a favor. Shepard agrees to help and uses coordinates given by Hackett to travel to the batarian prison on the planet Aratoht where Kenson is being held. Landing outside the prison, Shepard makes it past several security measures and prison guards. Shepard locates Kenson in the middle of an interrogation and frees her. Shepard and Kenson fight past more guards and escape the planet on a batarian shuttle. On the way to Kenson's team's base, she reveals that she and her team had entered batarian space to investigate rumors of Reaper technology orbiting on the fringes of the Bahak system. The team discovered a Reaper artifact they dubbed "Object Rho" hidden in the asteroids near the system's mass relay, and learned from it that the Reapers were rapidly approaching. The Reapers could use the system's mass relay, the "Alpha Relay", to strike anywhere in the galaxy. Kenson and her team started what they called "the Project" to prevent this from happening. Their plan was to hurl a large asteroid at the Alpha Relay and destroy it, delaying the Reapers' plans by months or even years as they are forced to find another relay. A consequence of this plan would be that the relay's supernova\-like explosion would obliterate the Bahak system and kill the 300,000 inhabitants of Aratoht. Since the stakes are so high, Shepard insists on seeing Kenson's evidence first. Kenson agrees and informs her team at the Project Base that she and Shepard are en route.

evidence.text:
Project Base was an installation secretly built by a Systems Alliance deep-cover research team on the asteroid 157-Golgotha in the Bahak system of the Viper Nebula. The team, led by Dr. Amanda Kenson, constructed it around a Reaper artifact embedded in the asteroid, dubbed "Object Rho." Their original intent was to study the artifact, but visions it emitted convinced them a Reaper invasion was imminent. Believing the Reapers meant to use the Alpha Relay to strike anywhere in the galaxy, the team resolved to destroy the relay. They acquired scrap engines and navigation technology through contacts on Omega and installed them into the asteroid so it could be launched into the Alpha Relay at the press of a button; this plan was "the Project."

During their study of Object Rho the entire team was indoctrinated. Eager to witness the Reapers' arrival, they abandoned the plan to launch the asteroid. After Kenson was captured by batarians on a scouting mission, Commander Shepard rescued her and returned her to Project Base with less than two days before the Reapers arrived. Realizing the team was indoctrinated, Shepard fought waves of Project Guards, Engineers, Elites, Pyros and a YMIR Mech before being knocked out by an energy pulse from the artifact, waking two days later with only hours left. Despite the team's opposition and Kenson's attempt to overheat the fusion core and destroy the propulsion systems, Shepard activated the Project and escaped moments before the asteroid struck and destroyed the Alpha Relay, annihilating the entire Bahak system and its batarian population.

evidence.text:
This Mass Effect 2 "Arrival" DLC Codex covered three subjects tied to Dr. Amanda Kenson's research. Object Rho was a large artifact rooted into the core of the asteroid in the 157-Golgotha system. Kenson's team catalogued three findings: it was shielded by a stasis-like barrier far stronger than a biotic field, resisting even laser drilling; its interior held a quantum stasis field rivaling Prothean mass relay technology that activated in response to threat and consumed enormous power apparently drawn from dark matter; and it broadcast on many spectra, including a quantum-entanglement-like pulse reaching into Reaper territory and an infrasound signal at frequencies linked to Reaper indoctrination. Kenson's lab monitored these signals hoping for a clue to defeating the Reapers.

Aratoht was a batarian colony in the Skyllian Verge, once claimed by both human and batarian governments until the Alliance withdrew after learning of its low atmospheric pressure and oxygen; batarians saw this as cowardice and colonized it with large numbers of laborers, many of them indentured servants or slaves. Cyanobacteria dumping had raised atmospheric oxygen by a fraction of a percent, which Hegemony propaganda trumpeted as eventual victory. Short-term profits came mainly from mining its metal-rich crust. The planet was rumored to hold military bases, with information tightly restricted by the Hegemony's Ministry of Information Control.

The Alpha Relay was dated using Dr. Kenson's revived method of analyzing dust trapped in relay gravity wells, which dated relays back millions of years, some possibly predating the Protheans. Kenson concluded the oldest known relay lay near the star Bahak in batarian space. Nicknamed "Alpha," it normally functioned as a standard secondary relay but, with certain controls adjusted, could draw immense dark energy to send cargo to sixteen other relays and even to the Citadel. Hegemony authorities kept this secret, fearing Council species would read a sudden route into their space as hostile intent.

evidence.text:
Fehl Prime was a human colony in the Terminus Systems and one of the top producers of pharmaceuticals for the Systems Alliance, which made its defense a military priority. The habitable planet had at least three moons, a desert-like colony region, and areas of massive bioluminescent fungus-like flora. It was also the site of an intact, functional Prothean interstellar communication device believed to be at least 70,000 years old, not being actively studied as of 2185.

In 2183, Fehl Prime was besieged by Blood Pack mercenaries led by the krogan Archuk. The Alliance sent several special forces squads, most of which were lost during the landing attempt. The only surviving unit, Delta Squad, defeated the Blood Pack, killing all except the krogan Brood, who was taken prisoner. Delta Squad was reassigned to guard the colony, which was rebuilt over the next two years and given a heavy anti-ship cannon and military-grade kinetic barriers.

When a jamming signal was detected, Delta Squad found and destroyed an alien bio-mechanical device on the colony's outskirts. Meanwhile a Collector ship arrived, incapacitating the colonists with Seeker Swarms and taking them aboard. Delta Squad fired a low-power shot from the defense cannon to stop the ship; the shot was deflected by its shields and the cannon was destroyed by return fire. Retreating to underground labs, the squad learned research there sought an antidote to the Seeker Swarms' paralytic agent, and with the captive Brood's help planned a counterattack.

As it departed, the Collector ship demolished the colony with its main proton cannon. Delta Squad boarded using Brood's shuttle and disabled the ship, but the colonists were lost; James Vega, acting squad leader, chose to rescue the asari Treeya, who held vital intel on the Collectors, rather than retrieve the colonists from the crashing ship. The Alliance erected a monument on Fehl Prime to the dead and later commended Vega for his choice, even though Commander Shepard ultimately ended the Collector threat and rendered the intel unnecessary. These events are dramatized in Mass Effect: Paragon Lost and referenced in Mass Effect 3.

evidence.text: Very little is known about the origins of the Prothean race; even the name and location of their homeworld has been lost to history. It is unknown precisely when Prothean civilization arose and how long it persisted, but one of their communication devices discovered on the planet Fehl Prime has been dated to as early as 68,000 BCE. After achieving spaceflight, the Protheans discovered the ruins of a previous spacefaring race, the inusannon, and from those ruins learned about mass effect physics and developed FTL technology. It gave them a significant advantage over their contemporaries, and they kept it secret for centuries. The Protheans would expand throughout the galaxy with the help of the mass relay network and make the Citadel their capital. Early in their development, the Protheans encountered a hostile machine intelligence which threatened to overwhelm them. To defeat the machines, the Protheans decided to unite all of the galaxy's sentient organic life under their empire. The other organic races were free to resist, but those that tried were crushed, and none ever managed to best the Protheans' might. In time, each of the subjugated races assimilated into Prothean culture and came to think of themselves as Prothean. United under a single cause, the Prothean Empire successfully held off the enemy machines in a conflict known as the "Metacon War". The Protheans extensively observed primitive species such as the asari, hanar, humans, quarians, salarians, and turians during their time. They cultivated species they deemed to have potential. Numerous outposts were placed on or near the primitives' homeworlds, with Prothean interference and activities kept beyond their subjects' comprehension. In time, the Protheans would have given these primitives the "choice" to be part of their empire.

evidence.text: Two years later, Fehl Prime has recovered and the Alliance has bolstered the colony's defenses with a heavy anti\-ship cannon and military\-grade kinetic barriers. Delta Squad, now a familiar presence to the colonists, is working to finish installing the defenses when Captain Toni orders them to investigate a strange jamming signal originating from the colony's outskirts. The squad is accompanied by asari anthropologist Treeya and the colonist Messner, who lends them his M35 Mako. At the signal's location the squad discovers an unknown alien device is its cause; Essex destroys it with his biotics, much to Treeya's chagrin. Taking a fragment of the device, Treeya leads the group to the site of an ancient Prothean communication system, which she uses to contact her mentor, Liara T'Soni. When asked what she thinks the device is, Liara reasons that it may be related to Reaper tech before the communication system is suddenly jammed. Treeya voices her doubts to the squad, explaining that Liara once worked with Commander Shepard and has since become obsessed with the myths about the Reapers. As the group begins to head back to the colony, the source of the new jamming is revealed: a Collector ship flies overhead toward the colony. The Collector ship deploys Seeker Swarms to incapacitate Fehl Prime's colonists, including Captain Toni, Christine, and her daughter April, who looks up to Vega as a hero. Only Delta Squad, Treeya, and Messner remain free, having arrived at the colony after the initial attack. Unable to prevent the colonists' capture, Vega decides Delta Squad has to disable the Collector ship so the colonists can be saved. They make their way to the colony's anti\-ship cannon and begin charging it, but Treeya suggests that a low\-power shot might be preferable in order to ensure that the colonists are not harmed. Vega agrees and the cannon is fired. Unfortunately, the shot is too weak and is deflected by the Collector ship's shields. Alerted to Delta Squad's presence, the Collector ship retaliates with a powerful laser blast that destroys the anti\-ship cannon, and releases dozens of Collector drones and more Seeker Swarms. As Delta Squad retreats to the secure underground labs beneath the colony, Kamille is snatched away by drones and Essex is paralyzed by Seekers while defending the labs' door.

evidence.text: **Messner** is a trader who arrives on Fehl Prime in 2185\. He presents himself as a traveling merchant who sells hardware around the galaxy, but secretly he is a Cerberus operative who has been tasked with investigating the recent disappearances of human colonies. |  | ***“Do you think I made the wrong decision?”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect: Paragon Lost** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | While delivering a shipment to Fehl Prime in 2185, Messner meets with James Vega and Treeya on a transport en route to the colony's underground research labs. He displays awe and gratitude to Vega for engineering the victory in 2183, making Vega think he is a huge fan, and announces he is proud to be a human. When they arrive, they are barred from entry; security for the labs has recently been tightened, and only authorized personnel are allowed entry. They return to the surface, where Delta Squad is assigned to investigate a strange jamming signal emanating from the outskirts of the Fehl Prime colony. Messner offers to drive them to the location using a M35 Mako he had brought in from off\-world from a volus. While he and Delta Squad find and destroy the source of the signal, an alien bio\-mechanical device, a Collector ship arrives at the colony and begins harvesting the population. Messner is the one who suggests using the colony defense cannons to take down the Collector ship. After Delta Squad fails to disable the ship owing to a low powered shot, Messner accompanies them to the underground labs to hide. Inside the labs, Delta Squad learns that the reason the security measures had been upgraded was to keep Messner out; the Alliance had identified him as a Cerberus operative and suspected him of trying to infiltrate the labs to steal research. Messner confirms this, and reveals that he was assigned by his superiors to investigate the disappearing human colony incidents and the Collectors' involvement. Vega is outraged and starts hitting him, but Messner talks him down, arguing that he and Delta Squad now have the same goal: to stop the Collectors. For the time being, they set aside their differences. When Delta Squad uses a ship piloted by the krogan Brood to break into the Collector ship in order to destroy its drive core, Messner shows his true colors. Before Brood can fire his ship's weapons at the drive core, Messner shoots him multiple times in the head. Without a pilot, the ship crashes and the remaining members of Delta Squad are taken prisoner. Later, Messner explains to Treeya that he had deliberately attracted the Collectors to Fehl Prime using the alien jamming device so that he could observe the Collectors firsthand and learn about their technology and motives. By sacrificing the colony and temporarily gaining the Collectors' trust, Messner hopes that he will acquire the information necessary to prevent future attacks and stop the Collectors. Messner then takes Treeya to a Prothean archive built into the Collector ship's systems. He had forced two colonists to try and access the archive, but the process had killed them; since Treeya had demonstrated her ability to interface with the Prothean ruins on Fehl Prime, Messner thinks she will be more successful with the archive and forces her to access it. They witness recordings of the Protheans' futile last stand against the Reapers on Fehl Prime, their subsequent transformation into Collectors, and their plan to render humans down into liquified genetic material to create a new Reaper. Messner records this intel on a bracelet, intending to take it to Cerberus. Before Messner can leave, the Collectors inform him that his usefulness has ended, and prepare a pod for his "ascension" with the other colonists. Messner tries to bargain with the Collectors, threatening to transmit the data he has gathered to the Alliance to use against them, but when the Collectors dismiss his threats and accuse him of bringing the "contaminant" Treeya aboard, Messner grabs her and throws her into the pod reserved for him. She grabs Messner's bracelet while struggling at the last moment. Just as Vega and Essex arrive to rescue Treeya, the pod is ejected out into space to remove the "contaminant". In the ensuing firefight between Delta Squad and the Collectors, Messner fires on Vega, but Vega disarms and stabs him. Vega demands Messner's intel on the Collectors; Messner tries to bribe and begs for his life but James, still angered by Messner's betrayal, refuses the offers. Treeya contacts Vega and tells him that she has the intel and her pod is beginning to enter Fehl Prime's atmosphere. As another wave of Collector drones descend and fire on them, Vega leaves Messner behind to die.

Vega chooses the latter. As Treeya's pod is retrieved, the Collector ship crashes into Fehl Prime's surface and explodes, killing all of the colonists aboard, who had hoped until the last second that Vega would come back for them.

evidence.text:
Mass Effect: Paragon Lost was an animated feature film produced by BioWare, FUNimation, T.O Entertainment, and Production I.G, screened in select theaters on November 29, 2012 and released digitally and on disc in December 2012. A prequel to Mass Effect 3, it followed the early career of Alliance Marine James Vega (voiced by Freddie Prinze Jr.). In 2183 the human colony of Fehl Prime, a major pharmaceutical producer, was attacked by Blood Pack mercenaries led by the krogan Archuk. Alliance shuttles were shot down; only Delta Squad survived, and Vega saved its commanding officer Captain Toni before dueling and helping kill Archuk, sparing his second Brood as a prisoner. Admiral Steven Hackett ordered Delta Squad to remain and defend the colony.

Two years later, with the colony rebuilt and fitted with an anti-ship cannon and kinetic barriers, Delta Squad investigated a jamming signal with asari anthropologist Treeya and the colonist Messner. They found an alien device; Treeya used a Prothean communication system to contact her mentor Liara T'Soni, who suggested Reaper tech before the link was jammed by an arriving Collector ship. Seeker Swarms incapacitated the colonists. The squad's low-power cannon shot failed, the cannon was destroyed, and squad members were killed or captured as they retreated to underground labs. There they learned Messner was a Cerberus agent, found Brood held as a test subject, and were attacked by a Praetorian incorporating Kamille's body. Brood led survivors to his hidden ship in exchange for repaying his debt to Vega; Messner shot Brood dead and the group was captured aboard the Collector ship.

Vega, Essex, and Milque escaped using a Seeker antidote Vega had secretly spiked into a shared drink, and planted antidote canisters to free the captured colonists. Treeya, forced by Messner to access a Prothean archive, witnessed the Protheans' transformation into Collectors and the plan to harvest humans to build a Human-Reaper. The Collectors turned on Messner; Treeya grabbed his data bracelet and was ejected in an escape pod. Vega killed the Collectors and left Messner to die, then faced a choice: evacuate the revived colonists or pursue Treeya and her intel. He chose the intel. The Collector ship crashed into Fehl Prime, killing all colonists aboard. On the Citadel, Vega was commended by David Anderson and Hackett, told the intel could yield an antidote and new weapons and that Commander Shepard was seemingly alive, and ordered to report for N7 training. He resolved to honor the lost colonists' sacrifice. The score was composed by Joshua R. Mosley and David Kates.

evidence.text:
The page collected the Codex entries on two extinct spacefaring races. Fifty thousand years ago the Protheans were the only spacefaring species in the galaxy and vanished in a swift galactic extinction, leaving ruins across many worlds; they were believed to have built the mass relays and the Citadel. Functioning Prothean "paleotechnology" was rare, most sites long since looted. Evidence of Prothean occupation appeared on the hanar homeworld Kahje and on Mars, feeding "interventionary evolutionist" theories among humans. The European Space Agency founded Lowell City on Mars in 2103; in 2148 prospectors near Deseado Crater discovered a buried Prothean observation post whose struggling mass effect core had caused local anomalies, proving humanity was not alone and triggering an international effort to translate its databanks. The post had been a biosciences station monitoring early humans, linked to platforms in Earth orbit and on the Moon.

A Prothean beacon was unearthed on the Alliance colony Eden Prime; it was a solid-state data-storage device from a galaxy-spanning comm network. The rogue Spectre Saren Arterius and his geth raided Eden Prime with the flagship Sovereign, causing hundreds of civilian casualties and badly damaging the beacon. During recovery the beacon fired an energy pulse into Lieutenant Commander Shepard, the Normandy's executive officer, who survived apparently unharmed before the device fell inert. The beacon implanted knowledge that produced confusing visions; understanding them required a "cipher," the cultural knowledge of a living Prothean, which might be impossible to obtain. Over three dozen fragile Prothean data discs had been recovered, a few partially restored, and were considered the best leads on Prothean culture.

Over 2,000 years ago explorers opened a mass relay to an unknown system and met the rachni, spacefaring insects guided by hive-mind queens on a toxic homeworld. Negotiation proved impossible and the Rachni Wars followed. The salarians uplifted the krogan, who could reach the queens in their lairs; when krogan fleets drove the rachni back to their homeworld and they refused to surrender, the krogan eradicated them from the galaxy.

evidence.text: **Quana**'s frozen surface is rich with heavy metals, and the planet's higher than average density suggests further mineral richness in the depths. The atmosphere is composed of nitrogen and carbon monoxide. The remains of a well\-developed Prothean mining infrastructure dot the planet. Abandoned mines are connected to dead cities by collapsed maglev lines. Unlike the crumbling skyscrapers of Feros, Quana's ruins are reasonably intact. Unfortunately, this only made it easier for looters to strip the silent necropoli of anything valuable.

evidence.text: Various Prothean ruins still survive on planets like Feros, Quana, and Therum, as well as many known yet unexplored sites in the Attican Traverse, with more unknown sites believed to exist elsewhere throughout the galaxy. While these ruins are surprisingly intact for their age, many were plundered long ago with time and generations of looters having picked their dead cities and derelict stations clean. Functioning examples of Prothean technology are rare. While hunting for rogue Spectre Saren Arterius, Shepard may discover Prothean data discs and ancient ruins on some uncharted worlds. The Commander can even receive a Prothean "trinket" as a gift from Sha'ira, but as Liara T'Soni claims, solid evidence on the Protheans is scarce. With the help of Shiala on Feros, Shepard also gains the Cipher, which is the key to fully comprehending the vision from the beacon. As the vision was meant for a Prothean mind, understanding it requires the individual to think like a Prothean \- to understand their culture, biological instincts, history and ancestral memory. This "cipher" then allows the individual to unlock the true meaning of the images, and understand the vision as it was meant to be seen. According to Shepard, the Cipher's effect on the vision is quite subtle, and Liara's Prothean expertise is necessary to make sense of the images. The Cipher also grants Shepard complete knowledge of the Prothean language. In addition to the technology they left behind, the Protheans left a greater influence through their in\-depth study of other races. Their work has had the greatest impact on asari, humans, and the hanar. A Prothean ruin on Eletania reveals that the elder race was monitoring humanity even in its early Cro\-Magnon form. The eventual discovery of a relatively small data cache in a ruined Prothean research station on Mars introduced humans to element zero and its follow\-on technologies, advancing the species' development by a few centuries at least. It also revealed the location of the Charon Relay, enabling humanity to become an interstellar civilization and a major galactic power almost overnight. The hanar, who call the Protheans "the Enkindlers", credit them with giving the hanar sentience and language, and worship them as a wise and benevolent race who allowed them to become civilized. Even more profound was the Prothean influence on the asari. One of the deepest secrets of the asari government is a collection of ancient asari relics held in a temple on Thessia. The relics show asari goddesses and their companions as Protheans. The asari were nurtured and, to a degree, uplifted by the Protheans, according to the last surviving Prothean, Javik. Even the asari aptitude for biotics was apparently cultivated by the Protheans. Javik also claims his people believed the asari would be a failsafe if the Protheans were exterminated—that the asari race's innate wisdom and patience combined with the head start gifted from Prothean intervention would enable it to succeed where its benefactors failed, defeating the Reapers in the next cycle.

evidence.text:
Feros was a habitable world, the second planet of the Theseus System in the Attican Beta cluster of the Milky Way, with two large moons, Orcan and Vardet. Two-thirds of its habitable surface was covered by the ruins of a crumbling Prothean megatropolis that had been picked over by looters many times since the Prothean extinction. Feros was a poor colonization prospect: little open ground remained for agriculture, the only sizable fresh water sources were the poles (tapped by decaying Prothean aqueduct systems), the dead cities were of uncertain stability, ground level was buried under a dozen meters of fallen debris, and the air was fouled by dust. Evidence suggested Feros had been a much colder world in the past.

In 2178, the human ExoGeni Corporation announced a permanent pilot colony on Feros to thoroughly explore the ruins. The pioneer settlement, Zhu's Hope, was placed on the upper levels of several intact skyscrapers, using surviving Prothean aqueducts and rooftop hydroponic gardens to support the population. In Mass Effect, Feros was visited after Shepard gained Spectre status, comprising the missions Feros: Geth Attack and Feros: The Thorian and assignments including Data Recovery, Geth in the Tunnels, Power Cells, Varren Meat, and Water Restoration. It became accessible again in Mass Effect 3 after Priority: Tuchanka.

evidence.text:
Knossos was a star system of four terrestrial planets and one gas giant in the Artemis Tau cluster. It held little of note beyond the industries of Therum and the helium-3 collection infrastructure on Archanes. At least two spacefaring cultures had used the system in pre-Council times: the zeioph kept crypts on Armeni, and the Protheans had a presence on Therum. The system's planets were Phaistos (first), Therum (second), Zakros (third), Armeni (fourth), and Archanes (fifth), most named for ancient Minoan cities and monuments.

Therum was the site of the mission Find Liara T'Soni, where Shepard recovered the asari archaeologist Liara T'Soni from Prothean ruins. The system also contained a carbonaceous asteroid where Navigator Pressly discovered an abandoned salarian fighter carrying a League of One medallion, and a metallic asteroid with platinum deposits. The system was likely named for the classical Minoan and later Greek city of Knossos, the oldest of the Greek city-states referenced by the Artemis Tau cluster; cut dialogue from Caleston's plotline stated Knossos was to be the name of the Prothean ruins where Liara was found.

evidence.page: The Art of Mass Effect/Alien Worlds
evidence.text: This page transcribes the fifth part and acknowledgements of The Art of Mass Effect (2007), with commentary by Casey Hudson. The section covers the game's landscapes and architecture, tracing how early combat-visualization paintings set an overall style before specific locations were developed. It discusses Eden Prime (shifted from green farmland to a red, ember-filled palette to darken the story's opening, keeping a cargo train), its train station, the Therum mining complex and mines, the Prothean tower where Liara is found, the Thorian's lair, and Feros (a human colony amid Prothean ruins, built largely from reusable parts). It also covers Ilos (changed from lush jungle to an ominous dead world) and its Archive of suspended Protheans, Noveria (a spaceport inspired by the Swiss Alps, made colder and more isolated), the ring-shaped Citadel Presidium and its grungier wards, docking bays and exterior, and Virmire (inspired by the islands of Palau, the site of Saren's oceanfront fortress). The acknowledgements credit the concept artists: Derek Watts, Matthew Rhodes, Sung Kim, Adrien Cho, Fran Gaulin, Mike Spalding, Mike Trottier, Michael Jeffrey, Sasha Beliaev and Mike Higgins.

evidence.text:
Find Liara T'Soni was a Mass Effect main-story mission acquired after Shepard gained Spectre status and command of the Normandy from Anderson. Liara T'Soni, an asari archaeologist renowned for her Prothean expertise and daughter of Matriarch Benezia, was being sought by Saren; her last known location was the Artemis Tau cluster. Anderson advised searching for the world with Prothean ruins, leading to Therum in the Knossos system. The mission was written by Chris L'Etoile.

Therum was a volcanically active world where the Mako could not survive contact with lava. Shepard fought through Geth Armatures dropped by a dropship, optional defense turrets around a refinery outpost, and a heavier push including Geth Destroyers and a Juggernaut, then faced a Geth Colossus on the road to the ruins. Outside the Prothean ruin, a dropship deposited snipers, shock troopers, Geth Hoppers, and an Armature; the entrance stayed locked until nearly all enemies were cleared.

Inside, Shepard descended by elevators and damaged platforms and found Liara floating trapped inside a Prothean security barrier she had accidentally activated while hiding from the geth. She directed Shepard to use a nearby mining laser: entering a code fired the laser to bore a tunnel past the barrier curtains, and a central console raised an elevator to her level. Freeing her triggered a tremor attributed to the mining laser causing a seismic event, and Shepard called the Normandy to the ruins. On the top level, Shepard fought a stand-off against geth and a Krogan Battlemaster before escaping the collapsing ruins as the Normandy hovered above.

Back aboard, Liara relayed her research, including a theory of recurrent galactic extinctions with the Protheans the latest to vanish, connected by Shepard to the Reapers and the Eden Prime vision. She joined the crew, considering the Normandy a safe haven from Saren, and offered her Prothean knowledge for interpreting the vision. If the mission was delayed until after Virmire, Liara instead believed Shepard was a hallucination until physically freed, cringed from the Battlemaster, and reacted angrily during the debrief as the squad's discoveries stripped away her decades of research. Recruiting Liara early unlocked unique interactions on Noveria and romance opportunities.

evidence.text: Located near the lawless Terminus Systems, the **Attican Traverse** is the true frontier of Citadel\-controlled space. The area contains many worlds once inhabited by the Protheans, and many mass relays are located throughout the systems of the Traverse. Colonies established in the Traverse are subject to constant raids and attacks from the nearby Terminus Systems, but the presence of multiple worlds both rich in resources and Prothean ruins, continues to draw colonizing interest. Though the Citadel officially claims the region as its own, the forces of the Terminus Systems have claimed many of the planets and systems to be under their control. Unwilling to engage in an all\-out war against the Terminus Systems, the Citadel has adopted a military non\-interference policy in the region. However, the Council makes no objection to the Systems Alliance's expansion in the Traverse, because the large Alliance Navy can settle unstable regions without the Council needing to get involved.

The Attican Traverse was a broad region of the Milky Way lying between Citadel-controlled space and the lawless Terminus Systems, regarded as the true frontier of the Citadel's domain. It contained many worlds once inhabited by the Protheans and numerous mass relays. Colonies established there faced constant raids and attacks from the nearby Terminus Systems, but the abundance of resource-rich worlds and Prothean ruins continued to attract colonists.

Although the Citadel officially claimed the region, forces from the Terminus Systems had seized many of its planets and systems. Unwilling to risk all-out war with the Terminus, the Citadel adopted a policy of military non-interference in the Traverse. The Council did, however, permit the Systems Alliance to expand there, since the large Alliance Navy could stabilize unsettled regions without the Council becoming directly involved. The region encompassed clusters including the Armstrong Nebula, Caleston Rift, Hades Nexus, Hawking Eta, Ismar Frontier, Kepler Verge, Maroon Sea, Ninmah Cluster, Nubian Expanse, Sentry Omega, Shadow Sea, and Styx Theta; the homeworld Suen; colonies such as Horizon, Mindoir, Ontarom, and Zorya; and space stations including Hephaestus Station and Jarrahe Station. The name "Attican" derives from Attica, the historical Greek region containing Athens.

evidence.text:
Caleston (Cut) documented the original version of the Mass Effect planet that was ultimately released as Therum; the wiki flags the material as cut content and not canon in any way. Caleston was the planet's name before a large amount of planned content was cut. Like Therum, it was where Commander Shepard would find Liara T'Soni, but it also had a hub area with several missions, assignments and characters called Throw Down, beneath which lay an element zero refinery that was the focal point of an ongoing gang war between the Miners' Union and the Cartel. Some distance from Throw Down, a set of Prothean ruins called Knossos sat inside a supervolcano caldera nicknamed the "Ring of Fire," which is where the player lands on the final Therum; neither name is spoken in the shipped game, though the star system is called Knossos. Cut dialogue and development images consistently depicted Caleston with a clear yellow/green sky rather than Therum's dark, stormy one, and Throw Down's administrator Tombiri claimed there were "hundreds" of Prothean ruins on Caleston, though most were not as well preserved as Knossos. Caleston was described as a moon, not a planet, orbiting Cernunnos, and the "Caleston DLC" (a misnamed prototype demo for Bring Down the Sky) placed it in a new Ankyra System in the Hades Gamma cluster.

Two surviving descriptions covered it. The Caleston DLC description read: "Geysers of molten suphur dot the rugged landscape of this volcanic moon, its atmosphere a toxic layer of sulphur dioxide," with Eldfell-Ashland Energy mining element zero left by an ancient meteor strike to make it "the largest source of starship drive core material in the Attican Traverse." The X06 trailer description called it "the hostile moon of Caleston," the largest satellite of Cernunnos, "wracked by constant volcanism, due to the tidal stresses from Cernunnos," with silicon-based native organic life whose populations "seem to be in decline."

Planned content included the missions Caleston: Last Man Standing and Find Liara T'Soni and the assignments Caleston: Redemption, Caleston: Reactivate Production and Caleston: Free Prostitutes. Caleston recurred in Mass Effect trailers up to release, variously placed in the "Perseus Cluster," the "Hades G Cluster," and, in a 2007 television ad, chosen by Shepard over a distress call from Noveria. Much of Throw Down's architecture was later repurposed as the final fight location in Bring Down the Sky, and its background story served as a basis for the criminal haven on Omega.

evidence.text:
The Terminus Systems lay on the far side of the Attican Traverse, beyond space administered by the Citadel Council or claimed by the human Systems Alliance. They were home to a loose affiliation of minor species united only by their refusal to acknowledge the Council's authority or adhere to the Citadel Conventions. That independence came at a cost: the region was fraught with war as governments and dictators rose and fell, and it was a haven for illegal activity, especially piracy and the slave trade. The prevalence of batarian criminal gangs made the batarian language a lingua franca across the Terminus. The region had no government, but the station Omega served as its trade capital.

At least once a year a Terminus fleet raided the neighboring Attican Traverse, typically small strikes against poorly defended colonies. The Council rarely retaliated, fearing that sending patrols into the Terminus would unify its disparate species into a common front and trigger a long, costly war.

Despite the dangers, Citadel races colonized the Terminus extensively; humans, turians, salarians, elcor, asari and volus all held sizable colonial presences, often fully independent of any interplanetary government. The region also encompassed the homeworlds of the quarians (Rannoch) and the vorcha (Heshtok). Before the Alliance expanded into the Voyager Cluster, the turians had mapped the Terminus in detail using an interferometric array stretching from the Attican Beta cluster to the planet Gromar. Its clusters included the Crescent Nebula, Omega Nebula, Far Rim, Perseus Veil, Sigurd's Cradle and the Shrike Abyssal, and its notable sites included Omega, the Mu Relay, the Omega 4 Relay and the Nemean Abyss. "Terminus" is Latin for "boundary stone."

evidence.text:
ExoGeni Corporation was an interstellar company specializing in planetary exploration and colonization. It funded several human colonies and in the process secured resource rights to worlds with potential undiscovered resources or alien technology, such as its colony on Feros. Juliana Baynham described it as a genius at "repurposing anything and everything." ExoGeni founded the Zhu's Hope settlement on Feros, funding it in exchange for valuable finds from the Prothean ruins, and converted an ancient tower above the Skyway into a base of operations, housing most researchers near the labs and using Zhu's Hope as a port.

Dissatisfied with returns from Feros until the Thorian was discovered beneath Zhu's Hope, ExoGeni "repurposed" the colony as a control group, deliberately allowing the colonists to be infected so it could study the Thorian's mind-controlling properties. The geth attack killed many employees and cut communications; once ExoGeni learned what had happened, it decided the situation was out of control and told its sole surviving representative, Ethan Jeong, that it planned to purge the colony to keep the secret. Jeong found ExoGeni held a dossier on Shepard. Depending on how Shepard handled Jeong, the company pulled or increased funding after the Thorian's destruction, with a Citadel news story covering the stock impact.

ExoGeni also conducted planetary studies: it was one of two Alliance corporations studying the Ontarom biosphere, ran a long-term plan to introduce water to Trebin, was involved in colonizing Chasca (supplied from Feros), and operated satellites billing ships for water-ice removal from Supay. A small facility on Nodacrux, led by a Dr. Ross, received Feros samples and found a way to make Thorian Creepers docile, but the Thorian's death sent them berserk; restricted communications delayed any rescue. The corporation also secretly researched Reaper technology with disastrous results: a survey team on Trebin died or became husks after excavating an artifact, and Cerberus collaborated with ExoGeni to deliver dragon's teeth to Chasca, converting that entire colony into husks.

In 2185 an ExoGeni researcher named Dr. Farrin hired the Blue Suns to guard Prothean artifacts recovered from Joab, but the mercenaries betrayed the team. If Feros remained viable, ExoGeni expanded advertising for third-stage colonization. By 2186 an ExoGeni team still on Feros studying Prothean remnants had expertise valuable to the Crucible project. In Andromeda, ExoGeni products such as M-Spec magnets turned up as low-value salvage, and Nakmor Drack recalled the company running dangerous mining operations. Known employees included Ethan Jeong, Juliana Baynham, Lizbeth Baynham, Gavin Hossle, Dr. Ross, and Dr. Farrin.

evidence.text:
Mars was the fourth planet of the Sol System. Once considered a prospect for terraforming and colonization, it became a quiet backwater after the discovery of faster-than-light travel. Its southern pole was made a historical preserve centered on the Prothean ruins found there, and immigration and development were restricted while the search for Prothean artifacts continued. Mars was explored by robotic expeditions for nearly a century before the first manned research stations arrived in the 2080s. The first permanent settlement, Lowell City, was founded in 2103 by the European Space Agency in Eos Chasma, and within a decade the US and China had established their own settlements. Satellites near Promethei Planum reported unexplained magnetic field shifts that gave the region a "Bermuda Triangle" reputation.

In 2148, a prospecting team led by Mateus Silva exploring near the Deseado Crater unearthed a subterranean Prothean ruin, the source of the disturbances. The ruins contained a malfunctioning mass effect core, several starships, and refined element zero. After a global translation effort, the structure was identified as a former Prothean observation and biosciences station set up to study Cro-Magnon humans on Earth. The observers' motives and conclusions remained unknown, but the fragmented data cache accelerated human sciences by roughly two hundred years, paving the way for FTL drives and later mass effect field technology. Some of the refined element zero fell into the hands of criminal triads on Mars, who used it to create the drug red sand, which may have taken its name from the planet's coloring. The mission Priority: Mars took place there, and Mars could not be mined. A cut Mass Effect DLC would have taken place inside the Prothean ruins and on the Bonestell Platform orbiting the planet.

N7: Archeological Dig Site was a Mass Effect 2 assignment on planet Joab in the Enoch system, unlocked after acquiring Jacob's loyalty mission opened the Rosetta Nebula. Scans showed Blue Suns mercenaries had seized an illegal archeological dig where a Prothean signature had been detected. Commander Shepard's shuttle landed and the squad fought successive waves of Blue Suns Legionnaires, Troopers, a Commander, and Lieutenant Locke, all of whom had to be killed to enter the site. Terminals and a PDA revealed the operation was run for ExoGeni Special Projects (chief researcher Dr. Farrin) under a transport-and-escort deal with Blue Suns co-executive officer Vido Santiago; Locke's orders were to rendezvous with Captain Vorhess aboard the MSV Strontium Mule in the Arinlarkan system once the artifact was secured.

The final chamber held a Prothean pyramid and a video log. Scanning it triggered a vision like the one Shepard received from the Eden Prime beacon, but ending with Collectors, which completed the assignment. Reading the PDA (or simply finishing the mission) unlocked the N7: MSV Strontium Mule assignment. Rewards included 125 experience, 7,500 credits and 500 element zero. A follow-up news report erroneously placed the missing ExoGeni team in the "Aeia Cluster."

evidence.text:
Therum was a distant but resource-rich industrial world in the Knossos System of the Artemis Tau cluster, the second planet of its system and claimed by the human Systems Alliance. Its abundant heavy metals fueled a manufacturing boom on Earth. Core samples containing fossils of simple silicon-based organisms indicated the planet was more habitable in the past, which may explain the many Prothean ruins on its surface, most of them already looted by mining corporations. Its capital was named Nova Yekaterinburg (New Yekaterinburg).

In Mass Effect, Therum was the setting of the mission to find Liara T'Soni, an asari researcher trapped inside a Prothean ruin during a geth attack while Commander Shepard pursued Saren Arterius. Shepard fought through the geth, including an Armature, extracted Liara from a Prothean security barrier, and escaped the collapsing dig site.

The page notes that Therum grew out of cut content. In early Mass Effect demo footage the location was a planet named Caleston where Shepard rescued miners trapped underground by a geth attack; the approach and the battle outside the entrance were the same, but the demo had Shepard question why the geth would deploy an Armature merely to kill miners. Under the name Caleston, the world was originally intended to host a full Eldfell-Ashland Energy mining facility with on-site workers and a seedy bar, as referenced in The Art of Mass Effect.

evidence.text:
Project Firewalker: Prothean Site was the final Firewalker assignment, acquired after Project Firewalker: Volcano Station. From data recovered at Karumto, Cerberus located Dr. Cayce's last known position on Kopis, a moon orbiting Makhaira in the Hades Nexus, where he had set out to excavate a Prothean site. Scans showed Prothean artifacts protected by a powerful energy barrier and hidden automated defenses.

The mission began with Shepard's squad in the Hammerhead. The kinetic barrier over the dig site was too strong for weapons, so it had to be brought down by destroying the generators powering it, following the power lines while evading Rocket Drones. Four eezo deposits could be collected outside the base. Once the last generator fell, the barrier dropped and the squad continued into the ruins on foot, passing dead Blue Suns mercenaries hired to guard the site.

Logs and datapads revealed the tragedy: Dr. Robert O'Loy had been indoctrinated by the Reapers and was leaking the team's data to a geth ship, and had made a deal with the Collectors, trading the Prothean find for the safety of his wife Helen's colony. Dr. Cayce discovered O'Loy's betrayal, killed him, then found the Reapers "still in my head" and resolved to destroy the relic and himself. Shepard hacked the console and examined the relic—similar to the one on Eletania—which glowed green and shrank to a manageable size, afterward displayed on the coffee table in Shepard's cabin. A follow-up email from Project Firewalker reported that an energy burst during the retrieval contained coded data advancing research on energy transfer and biotics, and that the artifact was inert and not dangerous.

evidence.text:
Race Against Time was the overarching main mission of Mass Effect, representing Shepard's ongoing effort to stop Saren Arterius. Saren was searching for the Conduit, an ancient relic dating to the Prothean extinction; through the visions burned into Shepard's mind by the Eden Prime beacon, Shepard came to believe the Conduit was a weapon capable of wiping out all life in the galaxy.

The mission appeared in the Journal after completing two of the three plot missions on Noveria, Feros, or Therum, when the Citadel Council requested a priority holo-meeting in the Normandy's comm room to share the latest intelligence on Saren. It did not correspond to any single point in the game and was completed only by finishing the game. Revealing the location of Ilos required completing Therum, Feros, Noveria, and Virmire in full.

The mission's name updated at story milestones: "Race Against Time" on acquisition, "Race Against Time: Sovereign" after meeting Sovereign on Virmire, "Race Against Time: Conduit" after speaking with Vigil on Ilos, and "Race Against Time: Final Battle" after passing through the Conduit and re-entering the Citadel.
